sections.vendors: Asda announced in January 2026 it is outsourcing George clothing buying and design functions, putting over 1,000 jobs at risk according to the GMB union. This structural change may shift George's sourcing strategy and supplier relationships as buying operations transition to an outsourced model.
sections.sustainability: George operates a five-pillar sustainability strategy covering responsibly sourced fibres, sustainable manufacturing, supply chain transparency, packaging reduction, and circularity. 75% of George's total cotton footprint is responsibly sourced, with all man-made cellulosic fibres targeted for FSC/PEFC certification.
sections.sourcing: George sources from Bangladesh, India, and China for volume lines. All George school uniforms are made with responsibly sourced fibres. The brand is a signatory to WRAP's Textiles 2030 initiative, committing to carbon, water, and circular textile targets across its supply chain.
sections.strategy: The outsourcing of George's buying and design functions represents a significant structural shift. This move could result in buying decisions being made by a third-party sourcing house, altering the direct supplier relationship model. The change is being contested by the GMB union.
sections.pricing: George remains one of the UK's most price-competitive supermarket clothing brands, positioned directly against Primark and TU. The outsourcing of buying operations may eventually allow for more aggressive cost negotiation if specialist sourcing houses are engaged.
sections.launches: George has continued to expand its school uniform and basics ranges with sustainability messaging. Recycled plastic clothing lines remain a focus, with Asda having previously committed to selling George clothing made from recycled plastic bottles.
sections.gossip: The 1,000+ job losses at George's buying/design function is the biggest George news of 2026. Trade commentators are watching whether outsourced buying will improve or harm George's speed-to-market and trend responsiveness — a critical issue for a brand competing in the value fast-fashion space.
soWhat: Outsourcing of George's buying function creates uncertainty for existing suppliers — approved vendors should proactively engage with both Asda and any newly appointed sourcing house to protect their position
If a specialist sourcing house takes over George buying, there may be a rationalisation of the supplier base — suppliers relying heavily on George volume should diversify their buyer portfolio now

75% responsibly sourced cotton target means ~25% of George's cotton is still uncertified — BCI-member suppliers in Bangladesh and India have a clear pitch to convert remaining conventional cotton volume
